The final pixel color $S^{(SG)}$ is computed by integrating the product of the BRDF, incident radiance, and cosine term [S2, unofficial]:

Source [S2], specifically in the 'Spherical Gaussian Shading' section, provides Equation (6): $S^{(SG)}(x, n, ω_o ; θ, γ) = ∫_{S^2} f_r^{(SG)}(x, ω_i, ω_o ; θ) L_i^{(SG)}(ω_i ; γ) G_c(ω_i) dω_i$. The text explicitly identifies $f_r^{(SG)}$ as the BRDF, $L_i^{(SG)}$ as the incident radiance, and $G_c(ω_i)$ as the approximation of the cosine foreshortening term. Thus, the evidence fully supports the claim.
